papers.title: Parametrization of stochastic inputs using generative adversarial networks with application in geology
papers.abstract: We investigate artificial neural networks as a parametrization tool for stochastic inputs in numerical simulations. We address parametrization from the point of view of emulating the data generating process, instead of explicitly constructing a parametric form to preserve predefined statistics of the data. This is done by training a neural network to generate samples from the data distribution using a recent deep learning technique called generative adversarial networks. By emulating the data generating process, the relevant statistics of the data are replicated. The method is assessed in subsurface flow problems, where effective parametrization of underground properties such as permeability is important due to the high dimensionality and presence of high spatial correlations. We experiment with realizations of binary channelized subsurface permeability and perform uncertainty quantification and parameter estimation. Results show that the parametrization using generative adversarial networks is very effective in preserving visual realism as well as high order statistics of the flow responses, while achieving a dimensionality reduction of two orders of magnitude.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用生成对抗网络对随机输入进行参数化，可迁移至生物力学设计中处理高维随机输入（如材料属性、几何不确定性），但未涉及植入物或生物力学具体问题。
llm.why_not_core: No implant or biomechanics application; no FEA surrogate or constraint handling; validation on subsurface flow, not biomedical.

summary_zh.motivation: 高效参数化高维随机输入以降低数值模拟成本
summary_zh.method: 使用生成对抗网络学习数据生成过程，替代传统统计参数化
summary_zh.result: 实现两个数量级的降维，同时保留高阶统计特征和视觉真实性
summary_zh.validation: 通过地下流问题的不确定量化与参数估计验证

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently parametrize high-dimensional stochastic inputs for numerical simulations by emulating the data generating process.
summary_en.method: A generative adversarial network is trained to generate samples from the data distribution, replacing explicit parametric forms.
summary_en.result: The method achieves two orders of magnitude dimensionality reduction while preserving high-order statistics and visual realism of flow responses.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on subsurface flow problems with uncertainty quantification and parameter estimation.

papers.title: Learning to Control Highly Accelerated Ballistic Movements on Muscular Robots
papers.abstract: High-speed and high-acceleration movements are inherently hard to control. Applying learning to the control of such motions on anthropomorphic robot arms can improve the accuracy of the control but might damage the system. The inherent exploration of learning approaches can lead to instabilities and the robot reaching joint limits at high speeds. Having hardware that enables safe exploration of high-speed and high-acceleration movements is therefore desirable. To address this issue, we propose to use robots actuated by Pneumatic Artificial Muscles (PAMs). In this paper, we present a four degrees of freedom (DoFs) robot arm that reaches high joint angle accelerations of up to 28000 deg/s^2 while avoiding dangerous joint limits thanks to the antagonistic actuation and limits on the air pressure ranges. With this robot arm, we are able to tune control parameters using Bayesian optimization directly on the hardware without additional safety considerations. The achieved tracking performance on a fast trajectory exceeds previous results on comparable PAM-driven robots. We also show that our system can be controlled well on slow trajectories with PID controllers due to careful construction considerations such as minimal bending of cables, lightweight kinematics and minimal contact between PAMs and PAMs with the links. Finally, we propose a novel technique to control the the co-contraction of antagonistic muscle pairs. Experimental results illustrate that choosing the optimal co-contraction level is vital to reach better tracking performance. Through the use of PAM-driven robots and learning, we do a small step towards the future development of robots capable of more human-like motions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及机器人控制与贝叶斯优化，与FEA代理模型或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA, no surrogate modeling, no implant or biomechanics context, no uncertainty quantification beyond Bayesian optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 实现高速高加速运动的安全控制
summary_zh.method: 使用气动人工肌肉机器人结合贝叶斯优化调参
summary_zh.result: 达到28000度/秒^2的关节加速度且避免极限
summary_zh.validation: 在真实机器人硬件上实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To achieve safe control of high-speed and high-acceleration ballistic movements on robotic arms.
summary_en.method: A four-DoF robot arm actuated by pneumatic artificial muscles is combined with Bayesian optimization for control parameter tuning.
summary_en.result: Joint angle accelerations up to 28000 deg/s^2 are achieved while avoiding dangerous joint limits.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation on the physical robot hardware demonstrates tracking performance on fast and slow trajectories.

papers.title: Trends in obesity prevalence among total hip arthroplasty patients and the effect on surgical outcomes, 2008–2016
papers.first_author_affiliation: Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, 3400 Spruce Street, Philadelphia, PA, 19104, USA

corresponding_authors.name: Kevin Pirruccio
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, 3400 Spruce Street, Philadelphia, PA, 19104, USA

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究肥胖对全髋关节置换术临床结果的影响，未涉及生物力学建模或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical outcomes study with no biomechanical modeling, no FEA, no stress shielding or micromotion analysis, and no implant design or validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨肥胖对全髋关节置换术患者手术结果的影响趋势。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析2008-2016年肥胖与非肥胖THA患者的临床数据。
summary_zh.result: 肥胖患者并发症风险更高，但手术量逐年增加。
summary_zh.validation: 基于大规模临床数据库的统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the trend in obesity prevalence among total hip arthroplasty patients and its effect on surgical outcomes.
summary_en.method: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from obese and non-obese THA patients between 2008 and 2016.
summary_en.result: Obese patients had higher complication rates, but the proportion of obese patients undergoing THA increased over time.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of a large clinical database.
